correctness.rationale: With the specified coproduct and D sigma = zeta sigma D, applying the relation to x forces D(x)=f(x^m); conversely the skew derivative with that generator value has the required relation on every monomial. Descent is precisely [N]_zeta x^(N-1) f=0, equivalent to forbidding a constant when r>0. The skew derivation annihilates every invariant polynomial; iterating on x^i gives the product of the j consecutive quantum integers with x^(i-j) f^j, or zero for i<j. A factor vanishes in any m-step iteration. Independently, put y=x^m and split into residues c mod m. For c>=j the j-step image in residue c-j is multiplication by y^(js) times a unit and a nonzero scalar; for c<j it is zero. The target residue has length ell+1 if c-j<r, else ell. The source has at least target length minus one, which is sufficient for js>=1, while s=0 is allowed only for r=0 so source and target lengths agree there. Summing max(0,target length-js) over c=j,...,m-1 recovers the stated rank including ell=js and ell<js. Rank one power determines s for a nonzero parameter; the Jordan second differences and the coefficient counts then give exactly the claimed partition frequencies. N<m leaves only zero, and at N=m a nonzero constant gives one block of length m. The frozen checker enumerates permitted parameters over prime fields, not arbitrary linear maps. The separate bounded probe `python3 -B /workspace/review_evidence/small_field_checks.py` verified quotient descent and all power ranks on 189 assignments with m=3 over F4, N=2 through 10; general exhaustiveness is by the generator proof.

On substitutions, leading degrees multiply under iteration; here images shift residue by one at each power. The inner twisted derivative description is a framework, not the claimed residue-rank theorem.

The exact frequency lets a reader count any nilpotent module profile over fields admitting the root without enumerating all parameter polynomials. This is an all-truncation structural result and not just a check of the single known cyclic boundary.
